asr.full_text: All right. Hello, everyone. Welcome back. My name is Katherine Gu. I'm the Head of Product for Digital Ad Assets at Celana Foundation. I'm here today with Andrei from Range. Andrei, welcome to the show. How are you doing? Yeah, thanks for having me, Katherine. Yeah, for the ones that don't know me, I'm Andrei, Co-Founder and CEO at Range. Yeah. Maybe tell us a little bit about Range. How long you guys been around? And also what are you doing specifically? RANGE started in 2012. We are based in Switzerland, but a global team with heavy U.S. presence. And RANGE is a treasury and risk platform for stablecoins and digital assets. We help companies such as Binance, Circle and also some of the largest banks in the world can integrate stablecoins safely and at the scale. Our risk infrastructure also powers some of the most innovative startups in Solana and beyond. So companies such as Squads, Jupyter, Camino, and many others. So to give you as well, a deeper dive in the product. So we have two main arms or solutions, one is the treasury side. We help companies unify their digital assets and stablecoin exposure, both for their treasury and also customer deposits and acting as a risk and control layer. On that front, we work as well with asset issuers such as stablecoin issuers, helping them understand and manage risk on the assets they put on chain with our Asset Intelligence solution which maps very clearly with the issuance capabilities of the SDP that we might have later. Another key element of our platform is our risk and payment infrastructure. Our transaction API's help companies on the compliance side providing real-time sanctions and compliant checks pre-transaction. We also offer more advanced kind of like risk and fraud solutions for Solana payments and transactions, basically, simulating the outcome of the transaction in real-time and trying to minimize both fraud, but also human operational errors. And to give you an example, like our footprints Solana, Squads is the absolute leader, of course, in non custodial stablecoin operations in Solana, every Squads transactions, would run a pre transaction simulation on the background to keep their users safe, and all of that is powered by Range. That's really cool. And we should definitely dig into a little bit around that and also just in the context for SDP, because in your joint announcement with us, you also mentioned about Range building explorer.money, which is this real-time Stablecoin Explorer. So maybe just tell us a little bit more in terms of exactly what does that real-time experience look like and how do you then help therefor to provide the visibility that enterprises need when they're building on STP? Yeah, I mean, to break it down into two like explorer.money, you can't think of it as a stablecoin explorer. And for us, this is a free-to-use, public good tool. You can access it from exploit.money and basically tracks all the stablecoin payments happening in the industry in real-time. We also displayed the relevant stablecoin entities blacklist information and different flows and spared of money first and foremost is about education and awareness we held companies and financially institutions that are maybe earlier in the digital assets and stable coin life cycle really understand what's out there. How are Stablecoins and stablecoin lifecycle really understands what's out there. Right? Like how are stablecoins and stablecoin payments follows to the happening and used in practice and where the activity is happening. So it's really about the location, and I would helping folks get to Speed, and it's part of money also used that sort of like more sophisticated users, developer teams, exchanges that to have a more of a unified, stable coin view on their activity. For example, let's say that you are a Central Exchange and you want to have a real-time monitoring of all the inflows of stable coins in your platform, you can use The Explorer for that. And beyond The Explorer, like I said, It is free, and everyone can use it, like, we offer data and analytics APIs for stablecoins on top of that, that some of our customers also use Got it. And maybe let's just dig in a little bit more just into this sense of real time because I want to understand, if you can quantify how real time is real time, especially as you mentioned earlier that, you know, for example, like squad radio ended before they run an actual transaction, they do the simulation. What is that back and forth? Like the general time it would actually take because just curious on that use experience. What does that look like? Yeah, I mean, a big element of risk and security is also UX, right? Like, you don't want to make risk compliance and security is also UX. You don't want to make a risk compliance and security checks be a problem, UX wise, because if not, users are forced to not do that. So when we talk about real time, our goal is always be on par with the block times of the networks that we operate in. Right? So in Solano, like fast block times of the networks that we operate in. In Solana, you know, like a fast block times to try to be in the order of 300 milliseconds but also depends on the workflow, right? Like for payments, for example, we need to be extremely fast, right? So the checks, the risk and compliance checks feel that they are happening in the background and don't affect at at all uh the user experience while providing these sort of like war rails uh both on the risk and compliance side on the other hand if let's say you are onboarding a user kind of like more of a address risk counterparty screening these are flows that are not necessarily requirement to be real-time, so we can also provide longer, more comprehensive checks on assets, on addresses, where there is not that limitation, but for payments and for transactions, we want to be on par with Solana Block so it feels there is invisible middleware that's happening in the background. Fantastic. And maybe let's tap into a little bit on the features within SDP because, as you know, on Solana development platform, the way that we are looking at all of these issuance of tokenization for real world assets, we leverage what we call token extension or token22 as the token program to support uh older enterprises just because of the fact that we know you know having regulated compliant uh issuance is super important so we wanna you know make sure that's been embedded from day one and there's many different extensions starting from kyc to you know metadata or like memo Fields and stuff like that. That's all being provisioned directly for clients to use inside SDP. Now, I think with that in mind, I'm curious to know, how does range... ...as you're doing your own compliance monitoring activities, how do you then leverage effectively... ...the token extension program itself and work in sync with us us to help to provide that good experience and good features for enterprise to use. We've been long supporters of Token2022 and token extensions in Solana. A bit of a trivia fact, we were the first sort of building disclosures and compliance mechanisms for confidential transfers to Token Extension. We actually are the first confidential transfer stablecoin payment in the whole history of Solana using token extension. Token extension capabilities we always find super exciting we've been always kind of tinkering with with what's possible in relation to SDP all our APIs like have full token 2022 support so to do token risk assessment to do address risk scoring transaction simulation sanctions screening all of them have have full support for token extensions on token22. One element that is super exciting for us as well is native transfer hook integrations. The idea is that we want to support and have our systems, our APIs natively embedded into transfer hooks, using as well attestation-based patterns with transfer hooks, using, as well, sort of attestation-based patterns with transfer hooks. So, you can have and deliver on the promise of having transactions and assets that have compliance and risk checks enabled natively into the programmability of the asset, and that's something that we've also been experimenting and exploring. And all our APIs, specifically like address asset and that's something that we've also been experimenting and exploring and all our APIs is specifically like address risk score can be fully embedded in a transfer hook flow so then you don't need to worry about calling third party APIs and have off-chain mechanisms and everything is baked in into the programmability of the assets, which we think is super exciting for institutional adoption of Solana assets. That's super cool. Having the really deep native integration is super important because I think this will really make a difference when it comes to the final user experience and the usability as people are building more custom type of tokens on-chain. I guess my last question kind of goes back to, I know you guys have been a long sort of, a participant and also like very valuable developer on the Solana developer ecosystem, you know, why build on Solana right, and especially I think, you know, as, as you probably have come across um I would say uh some of sometimes the misconception from institution be like uh if I want to have compliance and privacy I gotta do it on a private permission chain but since you guys are building every single bid on Solana right from the start you have a much better vantage point a view of Solana being that public permissionless chain but still able to cater for the compliance and privacy needs. So maybe talk to us about how you see that being available today and what does that look like down the road? Yeah. I mean, as you said, like we've been sort of strong supporters of Solana for a long time, I think from our personal standpoint, we just love the energy of the Builder Ecosystem in Solana. Like, compared to other ecosystems—I don't want to name names—but Solana teams are extremely pragmatic and really laser focused on building actual use cases for crypto and stablecoins. I guess also like on the personal side, our team has a strong sort of brass background, before starting Range in 2022, I was myself and Smart Contract Security Auditor focused on Rust Smart Contracts. So like Rust and sort of the whole developer ecosystem in Solana is just very close to our company V company DNA. So we enjoy the technical challenges around Solana and also like we're well-positioned to help companies tackle them. I think from a business standpoint, like building in Solana today is just super strategic. The two main KPIs that we see to understand what's our addressable market as a company is how many companies are building an ecosystem and how much transaction activity is performed by them. Solana is a leader in both year over year growth, and also user activity. So it's just, strategically speaking, it's a super important market for us and I think for everyone sort of building with crypto and digital assets. I think as well, like in the last 12 months, we've seen Solana becoming a neutral place for enterprises and institutions, building our chain, so this also creates a great opportunity for Rain to help these companies come on chain safely and at scale. We were big proponents as well, that you can bring privacy into public blockchain, which is where the liquidity and the users already are. And we think of privacy as a spectrum, right? I think we need to approach privacy with a very pragmatic mind set. And I think the Token Extentions capabilities in Solana are very good, that having a scale and a spectre of what privacy means for you, right full privacy can be, can be confidentiality, in terms of recipients, in terms of amounts, and I think what institutions, and financial institutions really need is a privacy that is also useful and pragmatic. it's not a black box that has the certain levels of privacy and confidentiality but also has disclosure mechanisms, has the required compliance and risk checks to be able to actually bring this to the world. And, you know, we are extremely excited to be a part of making this a reality in Solana. That's fantastic and that's really well put. So Andrea thank you so much for being on this podcast with me. We very much look forward to building out more enterprise-grade infrastructure together with you guys, so thank you. Yep no thanks for having me and I'm extremely excited about the SDP, making it easier for institutions and enterprises to adopt Solana, it's amazing so I'm extremely excited to be a part of that. Thank you, Kathrin.
